Hi Priya — great, thanks for confirming the 9/20 target and for sharing redaction guidance. A few technical notes so your team gets the ingest right first time: 

S3 transfer (preferred)
- We'll create a per-customer S3 prefix and issue presigned PUT URLs. Files should be uploaded under: s3://redwood-ingest/heliosys/hls-2027-045/
- Encryption: client-side encryption is fine; server-side AES256 is also supported. If you do client-side, please provide the encryption metadata file alongside the upload.

Preferred file format
- JSONL recommended. Each line = one record. Required fields: id, user_prompt, assistant_response (if available), timestamp, source_type. Optional: customer_truth_label. See attached s3-ingest-template.csv for mapping.
- Max file size: 1GB per object. If you have larger archives, split into day-based files.

PII / redaction
- If HelioSys sends redacted logs, please annotate which fields were redacted (e.g., email_address -> [REDACTED]) so we can account for gaps during eval. If you ask Redwood to run scrubbing, we will provide SOC-2 evidence and a short ingestion SLA addendum.

Eval & reporting
- After ingest, Redwood will run an automated baseline eval against the sample set and produce: token-level latency distribution, top-1/top-3 match rates against labeled responses, and qualitative failure examples (10 typical misses).
- Deliverable: PDF baseline report + CSV of scored records within 5 business days of successful ingest.

I attached a short presign/instruct file (s3-presign-instructions.txt) with example curl commands and our expected JSONL schema. If you want, we can create the S3 prefix and presigned URLs tomorrow morning — Tom, let me know which AWS account/email to grant temporary PUT access for.
